rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so I am pushing obfuscation aggressiveness up while protecting the hot numeric recursion loops (tak/takFP, fib/fibFP, fannkuch, spectral-norm) that dominate this benchmark's runtime. SUB and SPLIT get the highest security/diversity weights because they are near-free transformations that broadly obscure arithmetic and basic-block structure across all seven small functions. IBR and IGV are raised to add control-flow and data-reference diversity at modest cost, which is cheap given the tiny 721-byte text section. BCF and FLA remain moderately weighted with elevated RuntimeCost weights so the selector preferentially spares the tight recursive/loop kernels from their heavy overhead, applying them only where features indicate low loop intensity. ICALL stays moderate with the highest CorrectnessRisk weight since indirect-call transformation on this callback-light program offers limited gain relative to its risk. All passes remain enabled to maximize layered diversity; the cost and risk weights act as the safety brake rather than disabling any pass outright.
